Reference-only game logic data; not used as a runtime dependency (see CONTENT_RECOVERY_PLAN.md - must be translated, never executed as trusted server code). Not converted by this pass.

vectorRenderer.role: Rasterizes SWF vector shapes/timelines (DefineShape/DefineSprite) to per-frame PNG. Required because every inventoried source SWF in inhabitants/chicken and harvestable_resources/wood_tree is 100% vector art with zero embedded bitmap tags -- confirmed via tools/swf-extract-bitmaps.py, see 'bitmapExtractionAttempted' below.
vectorRenderer.reason: ~20MB Java application archive; not vendored to keep the repo small. A human/CI step must download and unzip this exact release (or a pinned equivalent) before re-running the pipeline. See tools/README-swf-pipeline.md.

frameLabelResolver.role: Parses the SWF tag stream directly (stdlib zlib/struct only) to compute REAL 1-based animation frame numbers for each named FrameLabel tag inside a chosen DefineSprite, by counting ShowFrame tags. This is more reliable than ffdec's -dumpSWF text output, whose per-line counters are nested-tag-list positions, not frame numbers.

sheetPacker.role: Packs a contiguous run of ffdec-exported per-frame PNGs into one horizontal sprite-sheet PNG matching the coUserver Spritesheet grid model (frameWidth x frameHeight x numFrames, single row). Fails if frames are missing or of inconsistent size.

bitmapExtractor.role: Diagnostic/fallback: extracts embedded raster tags (DefineBits*/DefineBitsLossless*) directly without rendering, for source SWFs that DO bake bitmaps rather than vectors. Run against both selected sources first; both reported zero bitmap tags (161 and 24 unextracted vector shape tags respectively), which is why ffdec rendering was required instead of a simpler direct-extract path.

assets.conversionMethod: ffdec -export sprite (rasterize) -> swf-frame-labels.py (resolve real frame numbers for each named state) -> build-sprite-sheet.py (pack each state's frame range into one PNG strip)

assets.sourceMappingAmbiguityNote: coUserver's Butterfly class had dead URLs literally named 'npc_butterfly__x1_...', but no npc_butterfly.swf exists anywhere in the fetched archive. Three inhabitant folders were candidates: batterfly (ruled out -- its own SWF is unambiguously the source for the separate Batterfly class below, confirmed by its internal SymbolClass name), swoonerfly, and caterpillar (a non-flying baby life-cycle form -- chicken.dart's EGG_ANIMALS confirms 'butterfly_egg' hatches into a 'caterpillar' item -- with no coUserver entity class of its own, so out of scope regardless). swoonerfly was resolved as correct with high confidence, not just by elimination: dumping npc_swoonerfly.swf's SymbolClass table shows its internal symbol names are literally 'npc_butterfly_fla.MainTimeline', 'npc_butterfly_fla.butterfly_side_2', etc. -- i.e. this SWF was authored as 'npc_butterfly' and only the folder/file was renamed to 'swoonerfly' at some point. As a second independent check, all 8 of Butterfly.dart's states resolved to frame ranges whose lengths exactly match the numFrames already hardcoded from the dead-URL era (see outputs below) -- a coincidental match across 8 independent values would be very unlikely.

assets.complexityNote: More elaborate than wood_tree/rock_metal, as flagged in the prior pass: trant_bean.as defines 10 discrete maturity-stage clips (beanTree_grow1..grow10, all exported with SymbolClass names) rather than wood_tree's 4, AND each growN clip is independently a real 10-frame timeline where the frame number is the tree's 'health' (tree.setHealth(health) in the source AS3) -- a combinatorial growth-stage x health design, not a single dimension. This maps directly onto coUserver's existing Tree.state/maxState harvest mechanic (state indexes the current maturity sheet's frames, maxState = numFrames-1), so no entity-code changes were needed -- only real numFrames=10 per stage instead of the old dead-URL era's guessed, mutually-inconsistent per-stage counts. A third dimension (per-pod bean_1..bean_N visibility, separately AS3-driven from a 'fruit_amt' value) is NOT representable by this single-image-per-state sprite architecture and is not modeled; each converted frame shows that growth/health combination's default authored pod visibility.
assets.conversionMethod: ffdec -export sprite (rasterize each named beanTree_growN symbol, 10 frames each) -> build-sprite-sheet.py

assets.complexityNote: The most elaborate of the four trees converted in this pass, and structurally different from bean_tree/bubble_tree: trant_fruit.as's 10 maturity clips (grow_1..grow_10) are NOT separately exported SymbolClass entries -- they were resolved by parsing the root timeline's raw PlaceObject2 tags for their instance names (grow_1..grow_10) and character ids directly. Each resolved grow_N clip is confirmed (via ffdec per-frame export) to hold only ONE frame at the top level; unlike bean/bubble, this tree's 10-level 'health' and fruit-count visuals are driven entirely by separately toggling dozens of nested per-leaf (fol_1..fol_maxfla, its own 10-frame timeline) and per-cherry (cherry_1..cherry_maxcherry, its own 3-frame timeline) child clips via AS3 -- a genuinely combinatorial per-instance system with no single equivalent top-level animation range, and not representable by this single-composited-frame-per-state sprite architecture (see per-output 'note' below).
